local_access.summary: The device is locally reachable over wireless ADB by any adb host on the LAN once paired — deliberately out of scope here; this project only identifies the device and does not open the debug channel.

device.name: Android Device (Wireless Debugging / ADB over Wi-Fi)
device.notes:
Android 11 and later advertise their Wireless Debugging (wireless ADB) endpoint over mDNS/DNS-SD when the user enables it in Developer options. This project does NOT connect to the debug channel or do anything with it — there is no web UI and no control surface here. We DISCOVER the device, recognise it as an Android phone/tablet with wireless debugging enabled, and draw a phone pictogram. Nothing more.
DNS-SD service types (published by adbd, per AOSP adb_wifi.md):
  _adb-tls-connect._tcp — the TLS connect server, advertised while wireless
    debugging is active. The connect port is DYNAMIC and discovered here,
    not a fixed 5555.
  _adb-tls-pairing._tcp — the pairing server, advertised only during a
    pairing session.
  _adb._tcp — the legacy cleartext service started by `adb tcpip <port>`.
The service instance name is "adb-" + the device serial (ro.serialno) plus a random suffix added by the mDNS backend (e.g. adb-35121FDJH000R8-xyMD0H); a QR pairing instance is "studio-"-prefixed and a code pairing instance is guid-prefixed. adb mDNS records carry no meaningful TXT data.
There is no admin_url: wireless ADB is a debug transport, not a web console, so there is nothing to deep-link to. The serial is embedded in the instance name but carries a random suffix, so the stable key is the mDNS hostname and the display name is the advertised instance name.

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. ADB's own TLS pairing (the 6-digit code or QR) is between the phone and whatever debugging host the user chooses — not this app.

factory_reset.effect: Not applicable: there is nothing on this app's side to reset. Turning wireless debugging off (or revoking pairings) is done on the phone and simply withdraws the mDNS advertisement.

methods.description: No provisioning by this app. The user enables Wireless debugging on the Android device; discovery is the passive mDNS advertisement of _adb-tls-connect._tcp.

setup.notes: Nothing for this app to provision. Wireless debugging is enabled by the user on the phone (Developer options → Wireless debugging); once enabled, adbd advertises _adb-tls-connect._tcp and the device is discovered passively. This app neither pairs nor connects — it only recognises the advertisement.

rejoin.notes: Re-enabling wireless debugging re-advertises the service on whatever network the phone is on; identity keys on the mDNS hostname, not IP.

testing.notes: No hardware exercised by this project. The discovery signature is taken from the public AOSP adb source and its adb_wifi.md developer documentation, not from a capture of a specific phone. The service types are published by adbd itself and are Android-specific, so identification rests on the AOSP definition rather than any one device.
